```{r save_all_rendered_outputs, include=FALSE}
# Export each chart and printed table while retaining the original R Markdown output.
# Only file-saving hooks are added; the analysis chunks below are unchanged.
export_project_root <- if (file.exists(file.path("data", "processed")) ||
                           file.exists(file.path("data", "split"))) {
  "."
} else if (file.exists(file.path("..", "data", "processed")) ||
           file.exists(file.path("..", "data", "split"))) {
  ".."
} else {
  getwd()
}
export_base_dir <- file.path(export_project_root, "outputs", "all_visuals", "03_hypothesis_regression")
export_plot_dir <- file.path(export_base_dir, "figures")
export_table_dir <- file.path(export_base_dir, "printed_tables_and_output")
dir.create(export_plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(export_table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Keep the built-in plot hook so figures still appear in the knitted report.
original_plot_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("plot")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) {
  for (source_file in x) {
    if (file.exists(source_file)) {
      # Knitr's filenames include the chunk label and figure number.
      destination <- file.path(export_plot_dir, basename(source_file))
      file.copy(source_file, destination, overwrite = TRUE)
    }
  }
  original_plot_hook(x, options)
})

# Also retain the original printed output and export it as readable text.
# This includes tables rendered by knitr::kable() in ordinary output chunks.
original_output_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  if (nzchar(trimws(x))) {
    label <- if (is.null(options$label)) "unnamed" else options$label
    path <- file.path(export_table_dir, paste0(label, ".txt"))
    cat(x, file = path, append = TRUE, sep = "")
  }
  original_output_hook(x, options)
})

# Save markdown/HTML table output when a chunk uses results='asis'.
original_asis_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("asis")
if (is.function(original_asis_hook)) {
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(asis = function(x, options) {
    if (nzchar(trimws(x))) {
      label <- if (is.null(options$label)) "unnamed" else options$label
      path <- file.path(export_table_dir, paste0(label, ".md"))
      cat(x, file = path, append = TRUE, sep = "")
    }
    original_asis_hook(x, options)
  })
}
```

# Load Data

```{r load_data}
# Find the project root whether knitting from code/ or the project root.
project_root <- if (file.exists("data/processed/pre_covid_clean.csv")) {
  "."
} else if (file.exists("../data/processed/pre_covid_clean.csv")) {
  ".."
} else {
  stop("Cannot locate data/processed/pre_covid_clean.csv. Open the project .Rproj first.")
}

# Read the two processed datasets without modifying the originals.
pre_path <- file.path(project_root, "data", "processed", "pre_covid_clean.csv")
post_path <- file.path(project_root, "data", "processed", "post_covid_clean.csv")

if (!file.exists(post_path)) {
  stop("Missing processed post-COVID dataset: ", post_path)
}

pre_covid <- read.csv(pre_path, check.names = FALSE)
post_covid <- read.csv(post_path, check.names = FALSE)

# Check the shared variables needed for comparisons.
required_columns <- c("PHQ", "GAD", "gender", "field", "race.2",
                      "yr_sch.2", "fincur.2", "age")

for (dataset_name in c("pre_covid", "post_covid")) {
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(get(dataset_name)))
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(dataset_name, " is missing: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
  }
}

# Confirm sample sizes.
data.frame(
  Dataset = c("Pre-COVID (2017–2018)", "Post-COVID (2022–2023)"),
  N = c(nrow(pre_covid), nrow(post_covid))
) |> knitr::kable()
```

# Clean Pre-COVID and Post-COVID Data

```{r analysis_01}
# Standardize survey periods and demographic categories across datasets.
pre_covid$Period <- "2017-2018 Pre-COVID"
post_covid$Period <- "2022-2023 Post-COVID"

post_covid$field <- as.character(post_covid$field)
pre_covid$field <- as.character(pre_covid$field)

post_covid$field[post_covid$field == "NotSTEM"] <- "Non-STEM"
pre_covid$field[pre_covid$field == "NotSTEM"] <- "Non-STEM"

pre_covid$gender <- factor(
  pre_covid$gender,
  levels = c("Men", "Women")
)

post_covid$gender <- factor(
  post_covid$gender,
  levels = c("Men", "Women")
)

pre_covid$field <- factor(
  pre_covid$field,
  levels = c("Non-STEM", "STEM")
)

post_covid$field <- factor(
  post_covid$field,
  levels = c("Non-STEM", "STEM")
)

race_levels <- c(
  "White",
  "Asian",
  "Black",
  "Hispanic",
  "Middle Eastern"
)

pre_covid$race.2 <- factor(
  pre_covid$race.2,
  levels = race_levels
)

post_covid$race.2 <- factor(
  post_covid$race.2,
  levels = race_levels
)

year_levels <- c(
  "firstyear",
  "secondyear",
  "thirdyear",
  "fourthyear+"
)

pre_covid$yr_sch.2 <- factor(
  pre_covid$yr_sch.2,
  levels = year_levels
)

post_covid$yr_sch.2 <- factor(
  post_covid$yr_sch.2,
  levels = year_levels
)

pre_covid$PHQ <- as.numeric(pre_covid$PHQ)
pre_covid$GAD <- as.numeric(pre_covid$GAD)
pre_covid$fincur.2 <- as.numeric(pre_covid$fincur.2)
pre_covid$age <- as.numeric(pre_covid$age)

post_covid$PHQ <- as.numeric(post_covid$PHQ)
post_covid$GAD <- as.numeric(post_covid$GAD)
post_covid$fincur.2 <- as.numeric(post_covid$fincur.2)
post_covid$age <- as.numeric(post_covid$age)

combined <- bind_rows(
  pre_covid,
  post_covid
)

combined$Period <- factor(
  combined$Period,
  levels = c(
    "2017-2018 Pre-COVID",
    "2022-2023 Post-COVID"
  )
)
```

# Adjusted Pre/Post Models

## Adjusted Depression Model

```{r analysis_18}
# Estimate the difference in depression scores between survey periods
adjusted_phq <- lm(
  PHQ ~ Period +
    gender +
    field +
    race.2 +
    yr_sch.2 +
    fincur.2 +
    age,
  data = combined
)

summary(adjusted_phq)
```

```{r analysis_19}

adjusted_gad <- lm(

)

summary(adjusted_gad)
```

```{r regression_tables}
# Present adjusted regression coefficients in compact tables.
regression_table <- function(model, outcome) {
  coef_table <- as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients)
  coef_table$Term <- rownames(coef_table)
  rownames(coef_table) <- NULL
  names(coef_table)[1:4] <- c("Estimate", "Std_Error", "T_Value", "P_Value")
  coef_table$Outcome <- outcome
  coef_table[, c("Outcome", "Term", "Estimate", "Std_Error", "T_Value", "P_Value")]
}

adjusted_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  regression_table(adjusted_phq, "PHQ"),
  regression_table(adjusted_gad, "GAD")
)

knitr::kable(adjusted_results, digits = 4,
             caption = "Regression Results")
```

# Paper Figures and Tables


```{r final_paper_export_setup}
# Make folders to save the tables and figures used in the final paper.
final_paper_dir <- file.path(project_root, "outputs", "final_paper")
figure_dir <- file.path(final_paper_dir, "figures")
table_dir <- file.path(final_paper_dir, "tables")
dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(table_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

save_paper_figure <- function(plot, filename, width = 8, height = 5) {
  for (extension in c("png", "pdf")) {
    path <- file.path(figure_dir, paste0(filename, ".", extension))
    tryCatch(
      ggplot2::ggsave(path, plot = plot, width = width, height = height,
                      dpi = 300, bg = "white"),
      error = function(e) message("Figure not saved: ", path)
    )
  }
}

save_paper_table <- function(tab, filename, digits = 4) {
  csv_path <- file.path(table_dir, paste0(filename, ".csv"))
  html_path <- file.path(table_dir, paste0(filename, ".html"))
  tryCatch(
    utils::write.csv(tab, csv_path, row.names = FALSE, na = ""),
    error = function(e) message("Table CSV not saved (file in use or folder blocked): ", csv_path)
  )
  tryCatch(
    writeLines(sub("<table", "<table class=\"paper-table\"",
                   as.character(knitr::kable(tab, format = "html", digits = digits, row.names = FALSE)), fixed = TRUE), html_path),
    error = function(e) message("Table HTML not saved (file in use or folder blocked): ", html_path)
  )
  invisible(tab)
}
```

## Assumptions: Regression Diagnostics (Residuals and Q-Q Plots)

Figure 1 combines residuals-versus-fitted plots and normal Q-Q plots for the adjusted PHQ-9 and GAD-7 regressions. The residual plots help assess functional form and possible changes in error variance; Q-Q plots show departures from the normal-error assumption relevant to conventional inference. Plotting uses a reproducible subset of up to 5,000 observations per outcome for legibility, while the adjusted regression models are fitted using all available complete observations. Neither diagnostic confirms independence or the absence of multicollinearity.

```{r final_paper_assumptions_residual_plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, dpi=150}
# These adjusted models were fitted earlier; do not refit or alter the analyses.
assumptions_diagnostic_data <- function(model, outcome, max_points = 5000L) {
  d <- data.frame(
    Fitted = as.numeric(stats::fitted(model)),
    Residual = as.numeric(stats::residuals(model))
  )
  d <- d[is.finite(d$Fitted) & is.finite(d$Residual), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) > max_points) {
    keep <- unique(as.integer(round(seq(1, nrow(d), length.out = max_points))))
    d <- d[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  n <- nrow(d)
  if (n < 5L) stop("Too few observations for regression diagnostics: ", outcome)

  outcome_name <- outcome
  residual_label <- paste0(outcome_name, " | Residuals vs fitted")
  qq_label <- paste0(outcome_name, " | Normal Q-Q")

  residual_data <- data.frame(
    X = d$Fitted, Y = d$Residual, Panel = residual_label,
    PlotType = "Residuals", stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  qq_data <- data.frame(
    X = stats::qnorm(stats::ppoints(n)),
    Y = sort(d$Residual), Panel = qq_label,
    PlotType = "Q-Q", stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  # Q-Q reference line goes through the sample's first and third quartiles.
  sample_quartiles <- stats::quantile(d$Residual, c(0.25, 0.75), names = FALSE)
  normal_quartiles <- stats::qnorm(c(0.25, 0.75))
  slope <- diff(sample_quartiles) / diff(normal_quartiles)
  reference <- data.frame(
    Panel = qq_label,
    Slope = as.numeric(slope),
    Intercept = as.numeric(sample_quartiles[1L] - slope * normal_quartiles[1L]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  list(residual = residual_data, qq = qq_data, reference = reference)
}

phq_diagnostics <- assumptions_diagnostic_data(adjusted_phq, "Depression (PHQ-9)")
gad_diagnostics <- assumptions_diagnostic_data(adjusted_gad, "Anxiety (GAD-7)")

# Two columns by two rows: residual plots on top and Q-Q plots underneath.
panel_order <- c(
  "Depression (PHQ-9) | Residuals vs fitted",
  "Anxiety (GAD-7) | Residuals vs fitted",
  "Depression (PHQ-9) | Normal Q-Q",
  "Anxiety (GAD-7) | Normal Q-Q"
)
plot_data <- rbind(phq_diagnostics$residual, gad_diagnostics$residual,
                   phq_diagnostics$qq, gad_diagnostics$qq)
plot_data$Panel <- factor(plot_data$Panel, levels = panel_order)
qq_reference <- rbind(phq_diagnostics$reference, gad_diagnostics$reference)
qq_reference$Panel <- factor(qq_reference$Panel, levels = panel_order)
residual_plot_data <- plot_data[plot_data$PlotType == "Residuals", , drop = FALSE]
qq_plot_data <- plot_data[plot_data$PlotType == "Q-Q", , drop = FALSE]

figure_assumptions_residuals <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes(x = X, y = Y)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5, color = "#356991") +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(data = unique(residual_plot_data["Panel"]),
                      yintercept = 0,
                      linetype = "dashed", color = "#555555", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_smooth(data = residual_plot_data, method = "loess", formula = y ~ x,
                       se = FALSE, color = "#D17439", linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_abline(data = qq_reference,
                       ggplot2::aes(slope = Slope, intercept = Intercept),
                       inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "#D17439", linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Panel, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Adjusted Regression Diagnostics: PHQ-9 and GAD-7",
    subtitle = "Top: residuals vs fitted (dashed = zero); bottom: normal Q-Q (orange = reference)",
    x = "Fitted score (top) / theoretical normal quantile (bottom)",
    y = "Residual (top) / ordered residual (bottom)"
  ) + paper_theme +
  ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
                 plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10))

print(figure_assumptions_residuals)

# Reuse the existing filename, so Run Project can still locate Figure 1.
# save_paper_figure() exports a 300-dpi PNG and a vector PDF.
save_paper_figure(
  figure_assumptions_residuals,
  "figure_assumptions_adjusted_regression_residuals",
  width = 10,
  height = 8
)

for (ext in c("png", "pdf")) {
  saved_path <- file.path(figure_dir,
                          paste0("figure_assumptions_adjusted_regression_residuals.", ext))
  if (!file.exists(saved_path) || file.info(saved_path)$size <= 0) {
    stop("The combined assumptions diagnostics did not save: ", saved_path)
  }
}
```

## Regression Results

```{r final_paper_regression_ci_table}
# Build the adjusted regression table with coefficients and confidence intervals.
model_ci_table <- function(model, outcome) {
  coefficients <- as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients)
  confidence_intervals <- stats::confint(model, level = 0.95)
  data.frame(
    Outcome = outcome, Predictor = rownames(coefficients),
    Coefficient = coefficients[, 1], Standard_Error = coefficients[, 2],
    CI_Lower = confidence_intervals[, 1], CI_Upper = confidence_intervals[, 2],
    T_Value = coefficients[, 3], P_Value = coefficients[, 4],
    row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE
  )
}
regression_ci_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  model_ci_table(adjusted_phq, "PHQ"),
  model_ci_table(adjusted_gad, "GAD")
)
save_paper_table(regression_ci_results, "table_02_adjusted_phq_gad_regression_ci")
knitr::kable(regression_ci_results, digits = 4,
             caption = "Regression Results")

paper_predictor_label <- function(term) {
  if (term == "(Intercept)") return("Intercept")
  if (grepl("^Period", term)) return("Survey period: 2022–2023 vs 2017–2018")
  if (grepl("^gender", term)) return("Gender: women vs men")
  if (grepl("^field", term)) return("Major: STEM vs non-STEM")
  if (grepl("^race\\.2", term)) {
    category <- sub("^race\\.2", "", term)
    return(paste0("Race: ", category, " vs White"))
  }
  if (grepl("^yr_sch\\.2", term)) {
    category <- sub("^yr_sch\\.2", "", term)
    category <- switch(category,
                       "secondyear" = "second year", "thirdyear" = "third year",
                       "fourthyear+" = "fourth year or later", category)
    return(paste0("Year in school: ", category, " vs first year"))
  }
  if (term == "fincur.2") return("Financial stress (per category)")
  if (term == "age") return("Age (per year)")
  term
}
paper_p_value <- function(p) {
  ifelse(is.na(p), "NA", ifelse(p < 0.0001, "<0.0001", sprintf("%.4f", p)))
}

regression_ci_publication <- regression_ci_results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Outcome = dplyr::recode(Outcome, PHQ = "Depression (PHQ-9)", GAD = "Anxiety (GAD-7)"),
    Predictor = vapply(Predictor, paper_predictor_label, character(1)),
    Coefficient = sprintf("%.4f", Coefficient),
    Standard_Error = sprintf("%.4f", Standard_Error),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("(%.4f, %.4f)", CI_Lower, CI_Upper),
    `p-value` = paper_p_value(P_Value)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Outcome, Predictor, Coefficient, Standard_Error, `95% CI`, `p-value`)
save_paper_table(regression_ci_publication, "table_02b_regression_publication_ready")
knitr::kable(regression_ci_publication, caption =
             "Regression Results")

```

## Interactions

```{r final_paper_interaction_table}
# Collect the period interaction results and format the table without extra row names.
extract_interaction <- function(model, outcome, comparison) {
  coefficient_matrix <- summary(model)$coefficients
  interaction_index <- grep(":", rownames(coefficient_matrix), fixed = TRUE)
  if (length(interaction_index) != 1L) {
    stop("Expected exactly one interaction coefficient for ", comparison, " / ", outcome)
  }
  confidence_interval <- stats::confint(model)[interaction_index, ]
  data.frame(
    Outcome = outcome, Interaction = comparison,
    # Drop the names that come from confint(). Otherwise R uses them as row labels
    # (for example, "2.5 %...1") when putting the interaction rows together.
    Coefficient = unname(coefficient_matrix[interaction_index, 1]),
    Standard_Error = unname(coefficient_matrix[interaction_index, 2]),
    CI_Lower = unname(confidence_interval[1]),
    CI_Upper = unname(confidence_interval[2]),
    T_Value = unname(coefficient_matrix[interaction_index, 3]),
    P_Value = unname(coefficient_matrix[interaction_index, 4]),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}
interaction_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  extract_interaction(phq_gender_interaction, "PHQ", "Period × Gender"),
  extract_interaction(phq_stem_interaction, "PHQ", "Period × STEM"),
  extract_interaction(gad_gender_interaction, "GAD", "Period × Gender"),
  extract_interaction(gad_stem_interaction, "GAD", "Period × STEM")
)
# Keep the four interaction rows in order, without the inherited row names.
row.names(interaction_results) <- NULL
save_paper_table(interaction_results, "table_03_period_interaction_results")
knitr::kable(interaction_results, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Interactions")

interaction_publication <- interaction_results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Outcome = dplyr::recode(Outcome, PHQ = "Depression (PHQ-9)", GAD = "Anxiety (GAD-7)"),
    Coefficient = sprintf("%.4f", Coefficient),
    Standard_Error = sprintf("%.4f", Standard_Error),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("(%.4f, %.4f)", CI_Lower, CI_Upper),
    `t-value` = sprintf("%.2f", T_Value),
    `p-value` = paper_p_value(P_Value)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Outcome, Interaction, Coefficient, Standard_Error, `95% CI`, `t-value`, `p-value`)
save_paper_table(interaction_publication, "table_03b_interactions_publication_ready")
knitr::kable(interaction_publication, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Interactions")

```


## Interaction Plots

```{r final_paper_interaction_plots, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
# Plot how PHQ and GAD scores vary by survey period, gender, and STEM status.
interaction_long <- combined %>%
  dplyr::select(Period, gender, field, PHQ, GAD) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(PHQ, GAD),
    names_to = "Outcome",
    values_to = "Score"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Outcome = dplyr::recode(
      Outcome,
      PHQ = "Depression (PHQ-9)",
      GAD = "Anxiety (GAD-7)"
    ),
    Period = factor(
      as.character(Period),
      levels = c("2017-2018 Pre-COVID", "2022-2023 Post-COVID"),
      labels = c("2017–2018", "2022–2023")
    )
  )

gender_means <- interaction_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Score), !is.na(gender)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Outcome, Period, Group = gender) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(N = dplyr::n(), Mean = mean(Score), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Comparison = "Gender", Group = as.character(Group))

stem_means <- interaction_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Score), !is.na(field)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Outcome, Period, Group = field) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(N = dplyr::n(), Mean = mean(Score), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Comparison = "STEM Status", Group = as.character(Group))

interaction_plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(gender_means, stem_means) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Outcome = factor(Outcome, levels = c("Depression (PHQ-9)", "Anxiety (GAD-7)")),
    Comparison = factor(Comparison, levels = c("Gender", "STEM Status"))
  )

figure_interactions <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  interaction_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(x = Period, y = Mean, color = Group, group = Group)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(Outcome ~ Comparison, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Men" = pre_color,
      "Women" = post_color,
      "Non-STEM" = pre_color,
      "STEM" = post_color
    ),
    name = "Student group"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Depression and Anxiety by Student Group",
    x = "Survey period",
    y = "Average score"
  ) +
  paper_theme

print(figure_interactions)
save_paper_figure(
  figure_interactions,
  "figure_02_gender_stem_interactions",
  width = 11,
  height = 7
)
save_paper_table(
  interaction_plot_data,
  "table_03c_interaction_group_means"
)
```
